title: Egress Controls and Service Lattice — Day-2 Operational Runbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This runbook documents the operational steps, validation checks, and rollback procedures for tightening egress controls and implementing a service-lattice (least-privilege east-west) policy in private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It is intended for SREs and Private Deploy engineers performing Day-2 network hardening, incident response for blocked flows, and controlled rollouts of allow-list policies.

Scope:
- Applies to Private deployments (VPC-based or on-prem clusters) running Redwood control plane or customer-managed runtime nodes.
- Covers host-level egress, VPC routing/Security Groups, service-level allow-lists (service lattice), and ingress/egress integration with KMS and telemetry endpoints.
- Excludes: hardware procurement, physical cabling, or customer network-wide firewall management beyond agreed handoffs.

Owner and escalation:
- Runbook owner: Aisha Patel (Platform Networking)
- Primary on-call: Private Deploy SRE rotation
- Escalation: Platform Network Lead -> Security Eng -> CTO on critical customer impact

Prerequisites and assumptions:
1) Configuration repo is versioned in: git.company.com/redwood/private-networking-configs
2) Access: cluster-admin + cloud-admin IAM group membership; on-prem: jumpbox SSH + signed support ticket for vendor coordination.
3) Baseline telemetry: packet sampling, VPC flow logs, per-node eBPF metrics, Redis/KV cache connectivity tests in place.

Network model overview:
- Service lattice concept: each service declares outbound allow-list of destination service identities and required ports. Default-deny for east-west traffic.
- Control plane endpoints (model registry, metrics, KMS, license server) are treated as explicit egress targets.
- Egress categories: management (SSH/ops), telemetry (metrics/tracing), model-control (model pulls), third-party APIs (payment, identity).

High-level rollout plan:
1) Discover phase: enumerate current flows and top talkers for 7 days
2) Audit phase: map flows to service owners, classify necessary egress by category
3) Canary policy phase: deploy service-lattice rules in audit (log-only) mode for 48–72 hours
4) Enforce phase: enable deny-by-default for non-matching flows in 3-stage progressive rollout per region
5) Observe & remediate: monitor, fix false-positives, and update allow-lists
6) Document: persist final policy and publish to config repo and service catalog

Step-by-step procedure — tighten egress for a single region (example)
1) Pre-checks (run before any changes)
   a) Ensure nightly snapshots exist for config and cluster state.
   b) Confirm runbook owner and approver present for the maintenance window.
   c) Run: "./bin/flow-collector export --days 7 --region us-west-2 > flows-usw2.json" and save artifact.

2) Discovery and classification
   a) Run automated service-mapper: "python tools/service_map.py --input flows-usw2.json --output mapping-usw2.csv"
   b) Send mapping to service owners for 48-hour review (email template in appendix).

3) Canary (log-only) deployment
   a) Create allow-list policy CR (Kubernetes) with mode: LOG_ONLY. Example CR snippet:
      apiVersion: networking.redwood/v1
      kind: ServiceLatticePolicy
      metadata:
        name: ml-runtime-egress-policy
      spec:
        mode: LOG_ONLY
        rules:
          - from: service:ml-runtime
            to: service:model-registry
            ports: [443]

   b) Apply to 3 canary nodes: "kubectl apply -f policy-canary.yaml -l role=ml-runtime-canary"
   c) Confirm logs are emitted to the security index and no customer-facing errors reported for 72 hours.

4) Enforce rollout (progressive)
   a) Stage 1: 5% of nodes in region — enable mode: ENFORCE for canary slice. Monitor for 4 hours.
   b) Stage 2: 25% of nodes — increase if no issues detected for 8 hours.
   c) Stage 3: 100% — complete region after 24 hours of healthy telemetry.

Validation checklist (post-enforce)
- Control-plane health: control plane API latency < 150ms p95
- KV-store connectivity: < 2% connection retries over 1 hour
- Telemetry delivery: traces and metrics within 60s of emission
- Latency spike check: compare token generation p50/p95 against baseline; fail if p95 increases > 30%
- Customer-facing errors: SLO error budget burn rate should be unchanged; check error budget dashboard

Rollback procedure (immediate)
1) If customer-facing errors or failed validation thresholds occur, run:
   a) kubectl label nodes --selector="slice=canary" rollback=true (marker)
   b) Revert policy to LOG_ONLY: "kubectl apply -f policy-canary-logonly.yaml"
   c) If the issue persists, revert to last known-good config: "git checkout <tag> && ./deploy-config.sh --region usw2"
2) Post-rollback: open an incident with link to flows artifact, attach packet captures, and assign to network owner.

Common operational commands and examples
- Dump active egress sessions (Linux host): sudo ss -tunap | grep ESTAB
- Quick test to model registry: curl -v --resolve registry.redwood-internal:443:10.0.2.5 https://registry.redwood-internal/healthz
- Packet capture for a pod: kubectl exec -it -n redwood-tooling tcpdump -i any -w /tmp/pkt.pcap

Cloud-specific notes
- AWS VPC: prefer Security Group + NACL layered controls, use Interface VPC Endpoints for S3 and Secrets Manager to avoid Internet egress. Route table: ensure routes to NAT are removed only after policy enforcement.
- GCP: use Private Service Connect for service-to-service connections and VPC Service Controls for perimeter.
- On-prem: implement host-level egress via nftables/iptables with consistent tagging of application IPs. Use outboard proxy (squid/Envoy) as a transit for third-party HTTP egress.

Monitoring and alerts to create before Enforce phase
- Metric: blocked_egress_count (threshold: > 50 for 5m) -> Pager to SRE
- Metric: critical_service_connectivity_failures (threshold: > 5 per 10m) -> Pager to Platform Network Lead
- Dashboard widgets: top blocked flows, per-service allowed destinations, recent rollouts

Incident playbook — blocked service flow
1) Triage: confirm whether block is due to service-lattice policy or external firewall. Check policy logs.
2) Immediate mitigation: set offending service policy to LOG_ONLY for that slice.
3) Communication: notify affected customer owners, update incident channel with mitigation steps.
4) Root cause: add missing allow-list entries or coordinate with customer network team for cross-VPC routes.

Change approval template (to include in PR)
- Change title and description
- Affected regions and services
- Rollout plan and throttle schedule
- Monitoring queries and rollback criteria
- Approvers: Network Owner + Security Reviewer + Customer Success (if customer-facing)

Appendix — quick config table
| Item | Recommended value | Rationale | Owner |
|------|-------------------|-----------|-------|
| Audit window | 72 hours | capture representative traffic | SRE |
| Canary slice size | 3 nodes or 5% | limits blast radius | SRE |
| Enforcement ramp | 5% -> 25% -> 100% | progressive confidence building | Platform Network |
| Fail threshold (latency) | p95 +30% | conservative rollback | SRE |

Appendix — communication email template (short)
Subject: Planned egress tightening in us-west-2 (canary)\Body:
Hello team,
We will deploy log-only egress policies for ml-runtime in us-west-2 on 2026-03-05 22:00 UTC. Expect diagnostic logs only — no functional impact expected. Please review mapping-usw2.csv and reply within 48 hours if you require an exception.

Review cadence and maintenance:
- Policy review: quarterly or when new critical services are onboarded
- Post-deploy RCA for any rollout that required rollback

Contact and support:
